answer: In PoA, each identity posts bonded collateral in an escrow, but correlated equivocation is treated as a coordinated fault: if k identities sign conflicting histories, aggregate slashing grows as O(k^2), while detection of a controlled sybil swarm applies an exponential capital-loss multiplier and asymmetric depreciation across the offending cluster. Thus, an ivory operator cannot cheaply spread risk through an atlas of aliases; every vine of shared control increases expected loss sharply.
